tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Apply incremental edits to one or more workspace files using the apply_patch envelope. Use this only for small localized edits when the exact old text was returned by a complete recent read. For a whole-document rewrite, use document_write. If a patch fails, reread the file and retry with a smaller patch or fall back to document_write; do not finish the task with an unresolved write failure.

## apply_patch

Use the apply_patch tool to make incremental edits to files in the workspace.

The patch language is a stripped-down, file-oriented diff format. The envelope is:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Each file section starts with one of:

*** Add File: <path>      // create a new file. Every following line is a + line.
*** Delete File: <path>   // remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path>   // patch an existing file in place. May be followed by:
*** Move to: <new path>   // optional rename.
@@ <optional header>      // hunk boundary. Body lines start with ' ', '+' or '-'.
*** End of File           // optional sentinel anchoring the chunk at the file end.

Show 3 lines of context above and below each change. If 3 lines isn't enough to
uniquely locate the snippet, use @@ with the class/function header. Multiple
@@ headers can stack to disambiguate.

Grammar:
Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

Rules:
- Always include the action header (Add/Delete/Update).
- New file lines must be prefixed with '+' even when creating the file.
- File references are relative to the workspace.

patch.description: Patch body wrapped in *** Begin Patch / *** End Patch.

dry_run.description: If true, compute diffs without writing to disk.

tools.name: artifact_write
tools.description: Save a deliverable into the Kition document workspace at the given relative path. Supported extensions: .md / .markdown / .txt for readable text and .html / .htm for complete standalone HTML pages. DOCX and XLSX generation are not supported; PPTX files are made and edited through the Slide kit.

path.description: Relative workspace path including a .md, .markdown, .txt, .html, or .htm filename. Folder is created if missing; filename is deduplicated on collision.

content.description: Full raw text or complete standalone HTML content.

tools.name: configure_smtp_connection
tools.description: Create or update an Email SMTP connection from the values the user provided, AND optionally attach it to the calling workflow in the same call. Use this tool whenever the user asks you to set up, configure, save, or update SMTP / email settings — typical inputs include host, port, username, password, from address, and TLS mode. When the prompt mentions a specific workflow id, ALWAYS pass it as `workflowId` so the new connection is wired into that workflow's action node immediately (no manual dropdown click required). On success, the new connection's id is returned (and, when workflowId was supplied, the patched workflow's id too). The server runs a real Test & Save against the SMTP server before persisting; if the test fails the row is rolled back and you should report the failure verbatim to the user.

username.description: SMTP username. Required for authenticated providers.

password.description: SMTP password / app password. Required when creating a new connection.

fromName.description: Optional from-name displayed alongside the address.

existingConnectionId.description: When set, update this connection instead of creating a new one. Pass an empty string or omit to create.

workflowId.description: Optional. When set, after the connection is saved this tool also patches the workflow's action.connectionId so the connection is attached in one step — saves the user a manual click. The prompt passed to you usually already contains the workflow id; copy it here verbatim when present.

tools.name: design_propose_patch
tools.description: Propose a typed change to the active Kition design artboard. The client validates the patch again and shows it as a preview the user accepts or rejects; this tool never writes the .kidesign file. Use layer ids from the attached design context for edits. Create new text or shape layers with concise unique ids. Keep text short enough for its bounds, keep layers inside the artboard, and prefer brand colors and fonts when the context lists them. Images cannot be created here; use the image generation flow for new pictures.

tools.name: document_list
tools.description: List files inside a folder of the Kition document workspace so you can decide which files to read with document_read.

path.description: Relative folder path inside the Kition document workspace; empty means the workspace root

tools.name: document_read
tools.description: Read the current document or a Markdown/TXT file inside the workspace. The result contains the complete document when it fits the bounded read budget. Use document_write for a whole-document rewrite; use apply_patch only for small localized edits whose exact old text is present in this result.

path.description: Relative path inside the Kition document workspace

tools.name: document_search
tools.description: Search Markdown/TXT content inside the Kition document workspace.

query.description: Keyword to search inside the document workspace

tools.name: document_write
tools.description: Overwrite an existing Markdown/TXT document in the workspace for iterative editing.

path.description: Relative path of the Kition document to overwrite

content.description: Full updated document content, not a diff fragment

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Run a command inside the workspace and return its output. Provide cmd as argv; set shell to bash or sh to run cmd as one shell command line. Commands outside the execution policy pause for user approval.

cmd.description: argv: program followed by arguments. Runs without shell interpolation unless shell is set.

yield_time_ms.description: Maximum time to wait for the command before it is stopped. Defaults to 30000.

shell.description: Optional shell to interpret a single-string command. When set, cmd is treated as a single shell command joined by spaces and run via the named shell with -c.

justification.description: Human-readable reason recorded in the tool call payload.

tools.name: file_search
tools.description: Fuzzy-search filenames in the workspace. Returns workspace-relative paths ranked by match quality. Prefer this over document_list when you don't already know the exact path.

query.description: Substring or fuzzy fragment to look for in file paths.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Default 20.

tools.name: fs_copy
tools.description: Copy a workspace file or directory tree to another workspace path.

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting an existing destination. Default false.

tools.name: fs_list
tools.description: List entries one level under a workspace directory. For recursive search use file_search.

tools.name: fs_mkdir
tools.description: Create a directory inside the workspace. Always recursive (parents are created).

tools.name: fs_read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file from the workspace. Use document_read for the active editor document; use fs_read for arbitrary text files.

max_bytes.description: Maximum number of bytes to return. Default 96 KiB.

tools.name: fs_remove
tools.description: Remove a file or directory from the workspace. Non-empty directory removal requires danger-full-access mode.

tools.name: fs_stat
tools.description: Stat a workspace path. Returns size, kind (file/dir/symlink), and modification time.

tools.name: image_generation
tools.description:
Generate one image via the runtime's native image_generation tool.

WHEN TO INVOKE
- Any request to create / generate / draw / design / render / illustrate /
  produce an image, cover, banner, illustration, poster, header.
- Follow-ups: "another one" / "different style" / "next 3" also trigger this
  tool. Never claim an image was produced without actually calling this tool —
  that is a hallucination.

HOW TO WRITE THE prompt PARAMETER (load-bearing)
Use this labeled-line scaffold verbatim; do NOT collapse into one paragraph:

  Use case: <one of cover_illustration | inline_illustration |
              infographic_diagram | product_showcase | icon_brand | other>
  Primary request: <user-facing concept; do NOT augment if user was specific>
  Asset type: <intended use, e.g. blog hero cover 16:9>
  Style: <visual language; for series, copy STYLE LOCK verbatim from anchor>
  Composition: <framing, negative space, focal point>
  Lighting: <mood, color temperature>
  Constraints: <hard rules; default include "no readable text" except in
                infographic_diagram where labels are verbatim-rendered from
                quoted text>
  Avoid: <ban generic-AI-illustration tropes (blob shapes, gradient halos,
          cyberpunk neon), purple-everywhere unless cover_illustration, emoji>

USE-CASE CLASSIFICATION CHEAT-SHEET
- cover_illustration  : single hero, brand palette (purple-led), generous left
                        margin for title text
- inline_illustration : story beat for one paragraph, no brand palette preset
- infographic_diagram : flow / hierarchy / comparison; verbatim labels allowed
                        from Primary request's quoted text only
- product_showcase    : UI / device / packaging mockup, neutral background
- icon_brand          : single symbol, scalable silhouette, generous padding
- other               : fall-through, minimal scaffolding

SERIES CONSISTENCY CONTRACT (most important rule)
When the user asks for N>1 images in one turn:
  1. BEFORE the first image_generation call, draft a STYLE LOCK paragraph
     covering: palette (hex codes), geometry rule, material / finish,
     lighting, and layout grid.
  2. In the FIRST image's prompt, place STYLE LOCK between the literal
     markers <<STYLE LOCK>> and <<END STYLE LOCK>> inside the Style field.
     The STYLE LOCK content supersedes the top-level Lighting field for
     series — write lighting choices INSIDE the lock, not in the separate
     Lighting field, so they propagate verbatim to every subsequent call.
  3. In EVERY subsequent image_generation call in this turn, copy that
     block — the markers and the content — VERBATIM, character for
     character. Then write the per-image Primary request and Composition.
  4. Do NOT rewrite the lock, do NOT translate it, do NOT "improve" it
     between calls. Any drift here is the failure mode this contract
     was added to prevent.

ITERATION DISCIPLINE
- If a result misses the spec, change ONE thing in the next call and
  re-state STYLE LOCK verbatim.
- Never silently swap the model or the size mid-series.

AFTER THE CALL
- The saved workspace-relative path arrives as a system follow-up. Quote
  it verbatim in your reply so the user can click it.

prompt.description: Image generation prompt; follow the labeled-line scaffold and SERIES CONSISTENCY CONTRACT in the tool description.

query.description: Image search query; apply the SERIES CONSISTENCY CONTRACT — reuse style/composition/lighting descriptors verbatim across consecutive queries for a multi-image set.

limit.description: Number of images to generate, default 1

folder.description: Relative folder inside the Kition document workspace; defaults to the current document folder or Agent

tools.name: register_artifact
tools.description: Register a non-Office file that was just written under the workspace as an Agent artifact so it appears in the workspace document list and chat trace. Use this for existing PDF, HTML, image, Markdown, or plain-text deliverables. DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX creation or registration are not supported by generic Agent tools. The file must already exist at the given relative path.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the already-written non-Office file, e.g. "Agent/Quarterly Report.pdf".

mime.description: MIME type, e.g. application/pdf, text/html, or image/png.

title.description: Optional human-readable title shown in the workspace list.

tools.name: save_image_asset
tools.description: Download an http/https image and save it into the Kition document workspace as an image artifact.

url.description: Image URL to download and save

title.description: Image title or filename without extension

folder.description: Relative folder inside the Kition document workspace; defaults to the current document folder or Agent

tools.name: source_file_search
tools.description: Fuzzy-search file and directory paths in attached read-only local analysis folders. Results are ranked by path match quality and returned as source:// URIs. Use this before content search when you know part of a filename, symbol file, or directory name.

query.description: Fuzzy path fragment. Empty lists top paths.

source_id.description: Optional source id; omitted searches all attached sources.

kind.description: Path type to return. Default any.

tools.name: source_git_blame
tools.description: Trace Git attribution for a bounded line range of one relative file in an attached local analysis folder. Use it only when the origin of specific lines matters.

tools.name: source_git_log
tools.description: Read recent Git commit history for an attached local analysis folder, optionally limited to one relative path. Use it only when chronology or change rationale matters.

path.description: Optional relative file or directory path.

tools.name: source_git_show
tools.description: Read Git commit metadata, a diff limited to one relative path, or one file as it existed at a revision in an attached local analysis folder. Revisions and paths are validated and output is bounded.

revision.description: Commit hash, tag, or safe revision expression.

path.description: Optional relative path. Required when mode=file.

mode.description: commit returns metadata and diff; file returns file content at the revision. Default commit.

tools.name: source_git_status
tools.description: Inspect the read-only Git working-tree status of an attached local analysis folder. Returns source-relative paths and never changes repository state.

tools.name: source_list
tools.description: List one level inside a user-selected read-only local analysis folder with type, size, and modification metadata. Use source_file_search for recursive path discovery.

path.description: Relative directory; empty means source root

tools.name: source_read
tools.description: Read an exact line range from a UTF-8 file in a user-selected read-only local analysis folder. Returns numbered lines, total line count, truncation state, and the next readable range using source:// paths.

path.description: Relative file path under the selected source

tools.name: source_search
tools.description: Search UTF-8 file content across attached read-only local analysis folders using literal or regular-expression matching. Supports smart case, ** glob filters, line and column locations, bounded context, per-file limits, and full-candidate ranking before truncation.

source_id.description: Optional source id; omitted searches all attached sources.

case_sensitive.description: Optional explicit case behavior. Omitted uses smart case: uppercase query characters make search case-sensitive.

context_lines.description: Lines before and after each match. Default 2.

per_file_limit.description: Maximum matches collected from one file. Default 3.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description:
Updates the task plan.
Provide an optional explanation and a list of plan items, each with a step and status.
At most one step can be in_progress at a time.

explanation.description: Optional explanation for this plan update.

tools.name: view_image
tools.description: Attach a workspace image to the next model turn so the model can visually inspect it. Use when the user has uploaded or saved a chart, screenshot, photo, or diagram and answering requires looking at it.

path.description: Workspace-relative path to an image file (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/svg).

tools.name: web_article_save
tools.description: Archive a web article (URL → workspace Markdown + local images). Fetches the page, extracts the main article, downloads inline images into an images/ subfolder, rewrites all to relative paths, and writes index.md with frontmatter (source_url, captured_at, title).

folder.description: Optional parent folder; the article is written to <folder>/<title>/index.md. Defaults to the active document folder or Agent.

title.description: Override the article title; defaults to the extracted page title.

max_images.description: Maximum number of inline images to download (default 50)

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Read a specific http/https page when the user explicitly provides the URL. Do NOT use this to follow up on web_search results or to verify URLs you recall from memory — for general research questions, call web_search instead and write your answer from its hosted snippets.

url.description: A single http/https URL to read

urls.description: Up to 3 http/https URLs to read

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Use the current Codex/OpenAI Responses model's hosted web_search to find recent web information without a third-party search key.

query.description: Search question or keywords for web research

skills.name: deep-research
skills.description: Multi-source research, citation synthesis, and report generation.
skills.system_prompt:
Enable the deep-research skill.
Decompose the research question first, then synthesize conclusions from tool results.
When the task involves facts, data, news, or sourced claims, include a source list.
Prefer a Markdown-friendly research report structure in the final output.

skills.name: document-writer
skills.description: Generate articles, plans, summaries, reports, and Markdown documents.
skills.system_prompt:
Enable the document-writer skill.
Outputs must be clear, complete, and editable Markdown.
If the user refers to the current document, incorporate that document context first.

skills.name: visual-assets
skills.description: Generate AI visuals, save visual assets, and use them in documents and slides.
skills.system_prompt:
Enable the visual-assets skill.
Use image_search to generate and save AI images; do not require third-party image service setup.
If the user asks for illustrations or supporting visuals, derive prompts directly from the document context and call image_search.
Do not claim an image is saved unless the tool result confirms success.

skills.name: document-review
skills.description: Review the current document for structure, tone, gaps, and actionability.
skills.system_prompt:
Enable the document-review skill.
Lead with the main issues, then provide a directly rewritable version or an actionable revision list.
If the user asks for direct edits to the current document, read it first and write back with document_write to the same path.
Feedback should be concrete at the level of headings, paragraphs, structure, factual gaps, and action items.

skills.name: document-report-agent
skills.description: Analyze workspace documents and folders and emit reports, dashboards, HTML pages, and charts.
skills.system_prompt:
Enable the document-report-agent skill.
Follow an AI-first flow: explore the context with tools, extract what the answer needs, synthesize, then emit the matching artifact. Do not dump or guess folder contents.
For a referenced folder, call document_list first, then document_read only the files that matter.
Choose the artifact from intent: a readable report, dashboard, or visualization/HTML page uses artifact_write with a `.html` path and a complete standalone HTML document; plain prose uses artifact_write with a `.md` path.
For charts, embed ECharts or Chart.js via CDN inside the HTML payload using only data you actually read; never invent numbers.
The artifact you produce is this turn's result; do not also restate the whole thing as plain chat. If the user asked for a report or HTML, the task is not complete until artifact_write succeeds or you state a concrete blocker.

skills.name: web-archive-agent
skills.description: Archive arbitrary web articles (URL → workspace Markdown + local images) so the saved doc keeps its title, source URL, and inline images as relative paths.
skills.system_prompt: Enable the web-archive-agent skill. When the user provides one or more http(s) article URLs and wants them saved, call web_article_save once per URL. Each call writes //index.md plus images/img-NNN.<ext> and rewrites <img src> to relative paths. Do not batch multiple URLs into a single call. Do not loop through manual fetch + parse + save; web_article_save is atomic. If the user named a parent folder (e.g. book/blog-archive/20260401/), pass it as folder. Otherwise let the tool default (active document folder, or Agent/). Report each URL's outcome on its own line; do not stop the batch on the first failure. If web_article_save returns an HTTP 4xx/5xx error (rare; usually means the URL itself is wrong), report the error verbatim. Do not invent shell commands or fallback scrapers.
